title: Imran Khan's Cornered Tigers
text:
The 1992 Cricket World Cup was held in Australia and New Zealand. Pakistan, captained by thirty-nine-year-old Imran Khan, was playing without its leading fast bowler, Waqar Younis, who was injured, and Imran himself was playing with a painful shoulder.

After five matches Pakistan had won only one. Against England they had been bowled out for 74, and were saved from almost certain defeat only because rain washed out the game and gave them a point. Elimination looked likely.

Imran told his players to fight like a cornered tiger, the animal that is most dangerous when it has nowhere left to run, and he wore a T-shirt with a tiger on it to the toss. He kept faith in young players, including the twenty-two-year-old batsman Inzamam-ul-Haq.

Pakistan won its remaining group matches, against Australia, Sri Lanka and New Zealand, and slipped into the semi-finals. There they beat New Zealand, with Inzamam scoring a rapid 60. On March 25, 1992, at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, they beat England in the final by 22 runs. Imran top-scored with 72 and took the last wicket himself.
lesson: When your team is on the edge of failure, give them a clear image of who they can be and back them with your own effort.
people: Imran Khan, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Pakistan cricket team
source: 1992 Cricket World Cup match records; contemporary press reports
caveat: Imran was criticized after the final for a victory speech that focused on his cancer hospital project and did not mention his team.
